**My thinking:**

I've farmed this land since I was young, helping my parents. My husband and I have about 8 mu. I don't read much, so I go by what I've seen work on our land and what the neighbors do. Around here, everyone grows winter wheat and summer maize — one after the other on the same fields. That's what this land is for. The seed shop in the township sells the improved wheat seed, the same kind my neighbor uses. For maize I always buy the hybrid bags — you get much better ears.

For fertilizer, I put down what I was taught. My father put a lot of urea on the wheat before winter and again at jointing. I do the same. I know the agronomist from the county station came around a few years ago saying we use too much, but if I put less and the yield drops, my family suffers. I'd rather use a bit extra than risk a bad harvest.

Water is the other big worry. We pump from the well three times for wheat — before winter sets in, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. For maize I water at planting and maybe once more if July is dry.

I'll rotary-till before wheat — our soil gets hard and compacted. For maize I just plant directly into the wheat stubble to save time and diesel.

My whole 8 mu goes into this rotation. I won't risk trying something new.
